balanceSheet.title: Balance sheet
balanceSheet.content:
Shareholders' equity is assets less liabilities; plotted against total liabilities to show leverage.

For KB Financial Group Inc.: equity that grows only through revaluations or share issues is not the same as retained earnings.

What to watch:

  • Liabilities growing faster than equity
  • Goodwill share of equity after acquisitions

cashDebt.title: Cash and debt
cashDebt.content:
Cash & equivalents against total borrowings (leases excluded unless noted).

For KB Financial Group Inc.: the DCF's net-debt bridge uses these balances at the latest balance-sheet date.

What to watch:

  • Net debt trend versus EBITDA
  • Refinancing dates and covenants in the filings

epsDps.title: EPS and dividends
epsDps.content:
EPS is net income per share; DPS is the cash dividend paid per share. Both are in major currency units.

For KB Financial Group Inc.: the payout ratio (DPS / EPS) shows how much of earnings is returned versus reinvested.

What to watch:

  • EPS growth versus net income growth (dilution)
  • Dividends funded from earnings, not debt

fcf.title: Free cash flow
fcf.content:
Reported FCF is operating cash flow less capital expenditure.

For KB Financial Group Inc.: as a bank holding company, operating cash flow is dominated by swings in loans, deposits and securities, not an owner-FCF DCF -- KB is valued on FCFE-at-cost-of-equity / residual income instead. Treat this chart as a cash-generation sanity check against net income, not a valuation input.

What to watch:

  • FCF persistently and structurally below net income
  • Large swings driven by balance-sheet growth rather than operations

niiPreProvision.title: Net interest income & pre-provision profit
niiPreProvision.content:
Net interest income (NII) is interest earned on loans and securities less interest paid on deposits and borrowings -- the core engine of a bank's earnings. Pre-provision profit adds non-interest income and subtracts operating expenses, before credit-loss provisions.

For KB Financial Group Inc.: NII tracks loan growth and net interest margin (NIM) in the Korean market; pre-provision profit is the cleanest read of underlying earning power before the credit cycle shows up.

What to watch:

  • NII growth versus loan book growth (margin compression or expansion)
  • Pre-provision profit trend versus reported net income (provisions explain the gap)

depositsEquity.title: Deposits & total equity
depositsEquity.content:
Deposits are the bank's main funding source; total equity (incl. non-controlling interests) is the capital base regulators and shareholders both watch.

For KB Financial Group Inc.: deposit growth funds loan growth without more expensive wholesale borrowing, and equity growth (largely retained earnings) underpins capital ratios and buyback/dividend capacity.

What to watch:

  • Deposits growing slower than loans (funding gap, reliance on wholesale funding)
  • Equity growth versus RWA/loan growth (capital ratio trend)

creditQuality.title: Credit quality
creditQuality.content:
Credit impairment charge as a share of pre-provision profit shows how much of the bank's underlying earnings power the credit cycle is consuming.

For KB Financial Group Inc.: a Korean bank's provisioning is sensitive to household and SME leverage and property-market conditions; a low, stable ratio is what supports the residual-income valuation's steady-state ROE assumption.

What to watch:

  • Ratio spiking well above its multi-year average (credit cycle turn)
  • Provisions persistently eating >30-40% of pre-provision profit

margins.title: Margins
margins.content:
Gross margin is revenue less cost of revenue; operating margin deducts operating expenses; net margin is after interest and tax.

For KB Financial Group Inc.: the spread between gross and operating margin is the cost of running the business; a widening spread with flat gross margin means opex is growing faster than sales.

What to watch:

  • Direction of operating margin over several years, not one
  • One-offs (impairments, disposals) that distort net margin

ocfCapex.title: Operating cash flow and CapEx
ocfCapex.content:
Operating cash flow is cash generated by operations; CapEx is cash invested in fixed and intangible assets.

For KB Financial Group Inc.: CapEx here is shown as stored (sign convention varies by ticker); the DCF splits it into stay-in-business and growth where disclosed.

What to watch:

  • CapEx rising faster than revenue
  • OCF that diverges from EBITDA

profit.title: Profit lines
profit.content:
Gross profit is revenue less cost of revenue; operating income deducts operating expenses; net income is after interest, tax and one-offs.

For KB Financial Group Inc.: the three lines together show where margin is made and lost between the top line and the bottom.

What to watch:

  • Operating income growing slower than gross profit (opex creep)
  • Net income far from operating income (interest, tax, one-offs)

revenue.title: Revenue
revenue.content:
Revenue is the top line: what customers paid for goods and services in the period, before any costs.

For KB Financial Group Inc.: the growth rate matters more than the level; compare it with the DCF's base-case growth path below.

What to watch:

  • Acceleration or deceleration in YoY growth
  • Whether growth is organic or acquired
  • Interim rows show seasonality

sbc.title: Stock-based compensation and share count
sbc.content:
Stock-based comp is the expense of equity awards; shares outstanding shows the dilution it causes net of buybacks.

For KB Financial Group Inc.: the DCF charges SBC as a cash cost and holds the share count flat, so this chart is the check on that assumption.

What to watch:

  • Share count rising while buybacks are advertised
  • SBC as a percentage of revenue
